STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of cooked sausage pieces (looks like chopped/bite-sized sausage or sausage rounds) on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-overhead angle. Only the plate in the centre is part of this meal; the plate at the left edge is not.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The square white plate is roughly 24 cm across its width. Vessel area ≈ 24 × 24 × 0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 490 cm²; using the ~23 cm usable width, I take about 480 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Cooked sausage pieces (about 17 pieces, a mix of rounds and chunks, some browned), a few small bits of yellowish fat or garnish near the top right (negligible).

STEP 4 - Area: Sausage pieces together cover roughly 12% of the plate area (about 58 cm²). Small garnish bits <0.5%. Total food coverage ≈ 12%, consistent with the scattered pieces.

STEP 5 - Volume: Each piece is roughly 1.5–2 cm in diameter and 1.5–2 cm long, so about 2.5–3 cm³ each. The pieces lie flat-ish in a scattered layer; outer envelope ≈ 58 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 87 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: 87 ml × 0.9 g/ml ≈ 78 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked pork/sausage ≈ 300 kcal/100 g. 78 g × 3.0 ≈ 234 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 17 small sausage pieces at ~4–5 g each gives roughly 70–85 g, matching the estimate. About 230 kcal is plausible for this amount of sausage. The scattered pieces cover only a small part of the plate, so a few hundred grams would be implausible.

Estimated total: about 78 g and about 235 kcal.
